q: every single visit to the OB they go, are you on insulin yet? Maintaining your diet,etc....because of your GDM and all. And when I correct them, they ignore me.
cx: 34 weeks; a specialist's note says otherwise.

q: honestly, shows in his lack of interest in taking birthing classes with me. He's participated in one online class.
cx: 37 weeks with her second, losing confidence in her husband as birth partner.

q: He told me, I was going to end up getting a c-section. That hurt because I've been consistent and healthy
cx: Her husband's prediction for the second birth.

q: he did assure me last night that he is devoted to my birth plan and will step it up as much as possible before the baby comes in terms of practice and class attendance.
cx: After a long talk with her husband.

q: What prep do you recommend? Books, courses, methods, physical prep, etc.
cx: Asking women who gave birth without pain medication and have no regrets.

q: Did you have any physical symptoms besides pain during labor and birth? Vomiting, nausea, shaking, chills, anything else?
cx: What she wants to know before her birth.

q: I gave birth 5 weeks ago in literally 3 hours, start to finish. Contractions started off manageable and within less than an hour they were insufferably painful and intense.
cx: Five weeks after her second birth.

q: I had to be induced with my first and got an epidural, so I didn’t really know how intense they can get!
cx: Why the second labour surprised her.

q: When I look it up it says 10 weeks, and I would technically be 4 weeks right now(one month since last day of previous period)but I also see multiple people saying they go weeks before that for blood work to keep track of hcg. What do I do?
cx: Positive test today, no OB, never had a smear.

q: It feels so big and like everything changed yet everything is the exact same and it’s a really weird feeling.
cx: The day of the positive test.
